title: Tiny worlds beyond Neptune still carry fingerprints from the Solar System’s birth
freshness: Published in The Astronomical Journal and announced by NASA on 8 September 2026, within the 15-day freshness window.
excerpt: Hubble and Webb found 27 previously unknown tiny worlds orbiting beyond Neptune, some among the smallest ever seen directly. Surprisingly, their surfaces resemble those of much larger objects, suggesting these distant leftovers have preserved clues about where and how they formed billions of years ago.
whyItMatters: These icy worlds are leftovers from the era when the planets were being built. Because they appear to have changed less than scientists expected, they may preserve a clearer record of the Solar System’s earliest days and help us reconstruct how the planets, including Earth, came together.
